paragraphs: Headquartered in Smithfield, Virginia, since 1936, Smithfield Foods, Inc., together with its subsidiaries ("Smithfield," "the Company," "we," "us" or "our"), produces a wide variety of packaged meats and fresh pork products primarily in the United States ("U.S."). Smithfield is an American food company that employs approximately 32,000 people in the U.S. and 2,500 people in Mexico. Smithfield's portfolio includes high-quality iconic brands, such as Smithfield®, Eckrich® and Nathan's Famous®, among many others. Smithfield is a majority owned subsidiary of Hong Kong-based WH Group Limited ("WH Group").

Good food. Responsibly.® At Smithfield, we are helping to feed a world of nearly eight billion people. Our products are found on tables everywhere. We provide families with wholesome, safe and affordable food while finding new and innovative ways to care for our people, communities, animals and planet. It is our responsibility and our promise. We make more than good food. Good is what we do.

We conduct our operations through three reportable segments: Packaged Meats, Fresh Pork, and Hog Production. We also conduct operations through two other operating segments, Mexico and Bioscience, which are aggregated and reported as "Other."

The Packaged Meats segment consists of our U.S. operations that process fresh meat into a wide variety of packaged meats products, including bacon, sausage, hot dogs, deli and lunch meats, dry sausage products (such as pepperoni and genoa), ham products, ready-to-eat products and prepared foods (such as pre-cooked entrees, bacon and sausage). Approximately 80% of the Packaged Meats segment's raw materials are sourced from our Fresh Pork segment. We market our domestic packaged meats products under a strategic set of core brands, which include: Smithfield, Eckrich, Nathan's Famous, Farmland, Armour, Farmer John, Kretschmar, Krakus, John Morrell, Cook's, Gwaltney, Carando, Margherita, Curly's and Smithfield Culinary. We also sell a sizeable portion of our packaged meats products as private label products. The majority of the Packaged Meats segment's products are sold to retail and foodservice customers in the U.S.

The Fresh Pork segment consists of our U.S. operations that process live hogs into a wide variety of primal, sub-primal and offal products, such as bellies, butts, hams, loins, picnics and ribs. In fiscal year 2025, the Fresh Pork segment sourced approximately 40% of its raw materials from our Hog Production segment and the remainder from farmers with whom we partner across the U.S. Approximately one-third of our fresh pork products, including the majority of hams, bellies and trimmings, is transferred to our Packaged Meats segment. Externally, we sell our fresh pork products to domestic retail, foodservice and industrial customers, as well as to export markets, including, among others, China, Mexico, Japan, South Korea and Canada.

The Hog Production segment consists of our hog production operations in the U.S., which produce and raise our hogs on numerous company-owned farms and farms that are owned and operated by contract farmers. Nearly all of the hogs produced by this segment are processed by our Fresh Pork segment. The Hog Production segment also sells livestock feed and grains and provides transportation and other ancillary services to external customers.

Mexico. In Mexico, we own a 66% interest in Granjas Carroll de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V. (commonly known as "Altosano"), which raises hogs and produces fresh pork products that are sold primarily to customers in Mexico.

Bioscience. Our Bioscience operations use raw materials from hogs that we process to manufacture heparin products, including an active pharmaceutical ingredient that mitigates the risk of blood clots. These intermediate products are sold to the healthcare industry for use in pharmaceutical drugs and medical devices.

On February 16, 2026, we announced that we had initiated the approval process to construct a new state-of-the-art combined fresh pork and packaged meats processing facility in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. The proposed facility would replace our existing 117-year-old plant currently located in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Our preliminary estimate of the proposed investment is up to $1.3 billion over the next three years. This investment is contingent on approval by the Company's board of directors as well as permitting and other regulatory approvals. If approved, construction is anticipated to begin in the first half of 2027 with production estimated to commence by the end of 2028. Additionally, if the project moves forward, we plan to accelerate depreciation and may incur other incremental costs related to closing the existing plant, which are currently under evaluation.

On January 20, 2026, we entered into an agreement to acquire all of the issued and outstanding shares of Nathan's Famous Inc. ("Nathan's") for $102.00 per share in cash. The acquisition is expected to be funded using cash on hand. Since March 2014, we have held an exclusive license to manufacture, distribute, market and sell "Nathan's Famous" branded hot dogs, sausages, corned beef and certain other ancillary products through retail outlets in the U.S. and Canada and Sam's Clubs in Mexico. The license is scheduled to expire in March 2032. The closing of the transaction is expected to occur in the first half of 2026, subject to satisfaction of certain conditions set forth in the merger agreement, including obtaining approval by the holders of a majority of the outstanding Nathan's common stock, approval from the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States ("CFIUS") and other customary closing conditions.

On January 29, 2025, we completed our initial public offering ("IPO") of 26,086,958 shares of common stock, representing 7% of the total outstanding shares, at a price of $20.00 per share. We issued 13,043,479 shares of common stock bringing the total number of outstanding shares to 393,112,711. The remaining 13,043,479 shares of common stock were sold by WH Group, through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary SFDS UK Holdings Limited ("SFDS UK"), our only shareholder at the time. WH Group granted the underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 3,913,042 additional shares of our common stock. On February 20, 2025, the underwriters partially exercised such option and purchased 2,506,936 additional shares of common stock from WH Group. We received net proceeds from the IPO of $236 million after deducting underwriting discounts, commissions and fees. Our common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "SFD."

On September 8, 2025, WH Group, through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary SFDS UK, sold another 22,461,452 shares of our common stock in a secondary offering. The sale did not affect the number of shares outstanding, nor did we receive any proceeds from the sale of stock by WH Group. Following this offering, WH Group owns approximately 87% of our shares of common stock.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business and Operations
Our results of operations are cyclical and could be adversely affected by fluctuations in the commodity prices for meat, livestock (primarily hogs) and feed ingredients.
Disruption of our supply chain could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
An inability to realize savings and efficiency gains could adversely affect profitability and we may be unable to achieve any or all of our financial and operational targets.
Changes in consumer preferences and failure to maintain favorable consumer perception of our brands and products could negatively impact our business.
Outbreaks of disease among or attributed to livestock can significantly affect production, the supply of raw materials, demand for our products and our business.
Product liability claims or product recalls can adversely affect our business reputation, expose us to increased scrutiny by federal and state regulators and may not be covered by insurance.
Our reliance on third-party service providers can have an adverse effect on our business.
Due to seasonality or changes in our promotional activities, our revenue and operating results may vary from quarter to quarter.
Significant increases in the cost of distribution could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our operations are subject to the risks associated with acquisitions, investments in joint ventures and divestitures.
We are subject to risks associated with our international sales, including disruptions to the worldwide economy due to changes in U.S. trade policy.
We depend on availability of, and satisfactory relations with, our employees.
We are subject to various risks relating to worker employment and health and safety.

paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be carefully considered. The occurrence of any of the following risks or of unknown risks and uncertainties may adversely affect our business, operating results and financial condition.

This risk factor summary contains a high-level summary of risks associated with our business. It does not contain all of the information that may be important to you, and you should read this risk factor summary together with the more detailed discussion of risks and uncertainties set forth following this summary. A summary of our risks includes, but is not limited to, the following:
•Our results of operations are cyclical and could be adversely affected by fluctuations in the commodity prices for meat, livestock (primarily hogs) and feed ingredients.
•Disruption of our supply chain could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
•An inability to realize savings and efficiency gains could adversely affect profitability and we may be unable to achieve any or all of our financial and operational targets.

•The food industry in which we operate is highly competitive, and our inability to compete successfully, or the effects of such competition, could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion and analysis includes the results of operations and financial condition, including year-over-year comparisons, for fiscal years 2025 and 2024. For discussion and analysis of fiscal year 2023, including a year-over-year comparison of fiscal years 2024 and 2023, see "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal year 2024. The information reflects all normal recurring adjustments which we believe are necessary to present fairly the financial position and results of operations for all periods included. Totals and percentages may be affected by rounding. Certain prior period amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation.

We are an American food company that employs approximately 32,000 people in the U.S. and 2,500 people in Mexico. We boast a portfolio of high-quality, iconic brands, such as Smithfield®, Eckrich® and Nathan's Famous®, among many others. We are an indirect, majority-owned subsidiary of Hong Kong-based WH Group.

We conduct our operations through three reportable segments: Packaged Meats, Fresh Pork, and Hog Production. We also conduct operations through two other operating segments, Mexico and Bioscience, which are aggregated and reported as "Other."
Our fiscal year is the 52-week or 53-week period which ends on the Sunday nearest to December 31. Fiscal years 2025 and 2024 each consisted of 52 weeks.
For a more comprehensive overview of our company and operations, refer to "Item 1. Business" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
The following are key factors that have influenced our results of operations in the past and/or may influence our results in the future.

The strategic initiatives we are executing across our segments are complemented and enabled by our strong balance sheet and ongoing operational investments, positioning us for future growth. We have several strategic initiatives to grow our business, reduce costs and enhance our profitability and margins. For a comprehensive discussion of our growth strategies, refer to "Item 1. Business—Our Growth Strategies in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We are focused on driving profitable growth through our Packaged Meats segment. Within the Packaged Meats segment, the primary factors impacting sales of our brands are household penetration, consumption levels, price point and product offerings. As a result, we have pursued strategies that we believe best align our products with consumer trends and behavior. We have shifted our portfolio towards a higher mix of value-added and margin accretive products while leveraging the breadth of our offerings to further penetrate across dayparts. We look to increase brand awareness and encourage consumer adoption of our products through product and packaging innovation and effective and appealing marketing strategies while maintaining our promise to consumers to offer high-quality products for every budget. We have also expanded to new categories and grown distribution of under-indexed brands in under-penetrated locations. In addition, we seek to increase sales in packaged meats products by driving volumes of our private label and foodservice products, by expanding our customer relationships and by offering quality selections across the value chain.

The U.S. packaged meats market is supported by long-term secular tailwinds, including consumer demand for high-protein diets, high-quality nutrition, product versatility and convenience. We expect these tailwinds to continue to drive increases in overall meat consumption. Nevertheless, changes in market trends and consumer preferences could adversely affect our results of operations.

In our Fresh Pork segment, the primary drivers of external sales are the consistent level of global pork consumption, our ability to maximize the value of each hog and our ability to leverage our different end markets including retail, foodservice, industrial and export channels. Through ongoing product innovation, we seek to appeal to ever-changing consumer preferences, including demand for convenience and smaller portion sizes as well as expanded interests in new and varied flavors. We also seek to capitalize on export markets as an outlet for increasing the value of raw materials through whole-hog utilization and by appealing to differentiated, global tastes and preferences.

Our cost as a percentage of sales varies based on fluctuations of raw material prices, as well as manufacturing, distribution and marketing costs. Raw materials are the largest component of our total cost of goods sold, with feed ingredients and hogs accounting for the majority share. The prices of feed ingredients, hogs and pork fluctuate based on market dynamics which can affect our margins. In addition, our distribution costs are affected by fuel prices, which also fluctuate based on market dynamics and may contribute to higher prices for feed ingredients and other inputs. We enter into hedging transactions for commodities such as feed ingredients, hogs and fuel when we determine conditions are appropriate to mitigate the inherent price risks. While this hedging may limit our ability to participate in gains from favorable commodity fluctuations, it also reduces the risk of loss from adverse changes in raw material prices.

We continue to optimize the size of our hog production operations and procure a greater mix of hogs from independent suppliers with market-based supply agreements in order to supply our Fresh Pork segment. We have reduced the size of our internal hog production from a peak of 17.6 million head in 2019 to 11.1 million head in 2025, which represents approximately 40% of the hogs processed by our Fresh Pork segment. We continue to explore opportunities to reduce internal production over the medium term.

We are pursuing best-in-class manufacturing principles in our plants by employing automation to redeploy labor to higher value tasks, increasing yields and driving efficiency by reducing complexity. In our logistics and distribution network, we have reduced transportation and warehousing costs by improving transportation carrier mix, maximizing utilization of our cold storage and trucking assets, improving supply and demand planning and optimizing inventory levels.

Our results of operations will continue to depend on our ability to (1) manage raw material cost movements through optimizing our hog production operations, hedging, forward purchasing, strategic sourcing negotiations and passing inflationary cost increases to customers, (2) operate our manufacturing and logistics footprint efficiently and competitively and (3) continue to attract and retain customers and consumers through effective sales and marketing spend.

paragraphs: 本公司設立於維吉尼亞州史密斯菲爾德，自1936年起，史密斯菲爾德食品公司（"史密斯菲爾德"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們"或"我們的"），與其子公司一起，生產各式各樣的包裝肉類與新鮮豬肉產品，主要在美國（"美國"）。史密斯菲爾德是一家美國食品公司，於美國僱用約32,000名員工，在墨西哥僱用約2,500名員工。史密斯菲爾德的產品組合包括高品質的知名品牌，例如史密斯菲爾德®、埃克里奇®與納坦斯著名®，以及其他許多品牌。史密斯菲爾德為香港-based WH集團有限公司（"WH集團"）的多數股權子公司。
好食物。負責任地。® 在史密斯菲爾德，我們致力於餵養近八十億人口的世界。我們的產品遍佈各處餐桌。我們為家庭提供健康、安全且價格合理的食物，同時尋找創新方式來照顧我們的員工、社區、動物與地球。這是我們的責任，也是我們的承諾。我們製造的不只是好食物。做好是我們的作法。
我們透過三個應報告分部進行營運：包裝肉類、新鮮豬肉與豬隻生產。我們也透過兩個其他營運分部進行營運，墨西哥與生物科技，這些分部被歸類並報告為"其他"。

包裝肉類分部包括我們在美國的營運，將新鮮肉類加工成各式各樣的包裝肉類產品，包括香腸、熱狗、冷切肉與午餐肉、乾燥香腸產品（如辣香腸與蓋奧納）、火腿產品、即食產品與預備食品（如預煮主菜、香腸與香腸）。包裝肉類分部約80%的原料來自我們的新鮮豬肉分部。我們在美國以一組戰略核心品牌行銷我們的包裝肉類產品，包括：史密斯菲爾德、埃克里奇、納坦斯著名、法農地、阿姆斯壯、農夫約翰、克雷奇馬爾、克拉庫斯、約翰莫雷爾、庫克斯、格瓦爾尼、卡蘭多、馬格赫麗塔、庫利的與史密斯菲爾德廚藝。我們也銷售相當多的包裝肉類產品作為自有品牌產品。包裝肉類分部的產品大多銷售給美國的零售與餐飲客戶。

新鮮豬肉分部包括我們在美國的營運，將活豬加工成各式各樣的原始部位、次部位與內臟產品，如豬肚、臀部、火腿、肋排、肩排與肋骨。在財務年度2025年，新鮮豬肉分部約40%的原料來自我們的豬隻生產分部，其餘來自與我們在美國合作的農場。我們約三分之一的新鮮豬肉產品，包括大多數的火腿、豬肚與邊角料，轉移至我們的包裝肉類分部。對外，我們將新鮮豬肉產品銷售給美國的零售、餐飲與工業客戶，以及出口市場，包括中國、墨西哥、日本、韓國與加拿大。
豬隻生產分部包括我們在美國的豬隻生產營運，這些營運在許多本公司所有的農場與由合約農場所有並經營的農場上飼養與培育豬隻。這個分部所生產的幾乎所有豬隻均由我們的新鮮豬肉分部進行加工。豬隻生產分部也銷售畜牧飼料與穀物，並為外部客戶提供運輸及其他輔助服務。
墨西哥。在墨西哥，我們持有Granjas Carroll de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V.（常見稱為"Altosano"）66%的權益，該公司飼養豬隻並生產新鮮豬肉產品，主要銷售給墨西哥的客戶。
生物科技。我們的生物科技營運使用我們加工的豬隻原料製造肝素產品，包括一種能降低血栓風險的活性藥物成分。這些中間產品銷售給醫療產業，用於製造藥物與醫療器材。

2026年2月16日，本公司宣佈已啟動批准程序，以建設一座位於南達科他州蘇城的新一代綜合鮮肉與包裝肉製造設施。此提案的設施將取代目前位於南達科他州蘇城的117年歷史廠區。本公司初步預估此提案的投資金額為未來三年最高達1.3十億美元。此投資取決於本公司董事會的批准以及相關許可與其他法規審批。若獲批准，預計2027年上半年開始動工，生產預計於2028年底啟動。此外，若此計畫進行，本公司計畫加速折舊，並可能產生與關閉現有廠區相關的其他額外成本，目前尚在評估中。

2026年1月20日，本公司與Nathan's Famous Inc.（"Nathan's"）簽訂協議，以每股102.00美元現金取得其全部發行在外股數。此收購預計將使用現金支應。自2014年3月起，本公司已持有獨家許可，製造、分銷、行銷與銷售"Nathan's Famous"品牌的熱狗、香腸、火腿及某些其他相關產品，透過美國與加拿大零售通路及墨西哥的Sam's Clubs。此許可預計於2032年3月到期。交易的完成預計於2026年上半年，視合併協議中所列條件是否達成而定，包括取得Nathan's普通股持有人過半數同意、美國對外投資委員會（"CFIUS"）的批准及其他慣例性交易條件。

2025年1月29日，本公司完成首次公開發行（"IPO"）26,086,958股普通股，代表總發行股數的7%，每股價格為20.00美元。本公司發行13,043,479股普通股，使總發行股數增至393,112,711股。剩餘13,043,479股普通股由WH Group透過其間接全資子公司SFDS UK Holdings Limited（"SFDS UK"），本公司當時唯一股東出售。WH Group給予經紀商30日選擇權，以購買最多3,913,042股本公司普通股。2025年2月20日，經紀商部分行使此選擇權，購買2,506,936股普通股自WH Group。本公司從IPO收到淨資金236百萬美元，扣除經紀商折扣、佣金及費用後。本公司普通股於納斯達克全球選選市場上市，股票代碼為"SFD."
2025年9月8日，WH Group透過其間接全資子公司SFDS UK，出售另一22,461,452股本公司普通股於次級發行。此次出售未影響發行股數，本公司亦未從WH Group出售股票中獲得資金。此發行後，WH Group持有本公司約87%的普通股。
本公司於過去幾年已採取多項行動，以重整並優化我們的豬隻生產業務規模，包括停止某些農場運作、終止與績效不佳的契約農場的協議，並縮減我們的豬隻生產業務規模（"豬隻生產改革"）。最近，我們的行動包括以下戰略措施：

paragraphs: 下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，應與本年度10-K申報表第二部分第8項所載之合併財務報表及附註一併閱讀。此討論與分析包含營運成果與財務狀況，包括與去年同期之比較，為財務年度2025及2024之資料。有關財務年度2023之討論與分析，包括與財務年度2024及2023之比較，請參閱我們財務年度2024之10-K申報表所載之「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」。資訊已包含所有正常重複調整，我們認為此為呈現各期間財務狀況與營運成果之必要調整。總額與百分比可能因四捨五入而有所影響。某些前一時期之金額已重新分類，以符合當期之呈現方式。
我們為一家美國食品公司，於美國僱用約32,000名員工，於墨西哥僱用約2,500名員工。我們擁有高品質、具有代表性的知名品牌組合，例如Smithfield®、Eckrich®與Nathan's Famous®，以及其他許多品牌。我們為香港-based WH Group所間接擁有大股權之子公司。
我們透過三個應報告分部進行營運：包裝肉類、鮮豬肉及豬隻生產。我們亦透過兩個其他營運分部，墨西哥與生物科技，進行營運，並合併報告為「其他」。
我們之財務年度為結訖於12月31日最近之星期日之52週或53週期間。財務年度2025與2024各自皆為52週。
如需更完整的公司與營運概覽，請參閱本年度10-K申報表之「項目1.業務」。
以下為過去影響我們營運成果，或可能影響我們未來營運成果之關鍵因素。
我們在各分部執行之戰略方案，配合我們強固之資產負債表與持續之營運投資，使我們能為未來成長做準備。我們有數項戰略方案，用以擴張業務、降低成本並提高我們之獲利能力與毛利率。如需完整討論我們之成長策略，請參閱本年度10-K申報表之「項目1.業務—我們之成長策略」。

我們專注於透過包裝肉類分部推動獲利性成長。在包裝肉類分部內，影響我們品牌銷售之主要因素為家庭滲透率、消費水平、價格點與產品組合。因此，我們已執行我們認為最能與消費者趨勢與行為對應之策略。我們已將產品組合轉向較高比例之附加價值與毛利率提升產品，同時利用我們產品組合之廣度進一步滲透各時段。我們期望透過產品與包裝創新及有效且吸引人的行銷策略，提高品牌知名度並鼓勵消費者採用我們之產品，同時維持我們對消費者承諾提供高品質產品，符合各預算層面。我們亦已擴展至新類別，並在滲透不足地區成長較低指標品牌之通路。此外，我們亦尋求透過提高私標與餐飲產品之銷售量、擴大客戶關係及提供價值鏈中之高品質選擇，來增加包裝肉類產品之銷售。
美國包裝肉類市場受到長期基礎性成長動能支撐，包括消費者對高蛋白飲食、高品質營養、產品多樣性與便利性的需求。我們預期這些動能會持續推動整體肉類消費量增加。然而，市場趨勢與消費者偏好變動可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
在我們的鮮豬肉分部，外部銷售的主要驅動因素為全球豬肉消費量的穩定水平、我們最大化每頭豬價值的能力，以及我們利用不同終端市場（包括零售、餐飲、工業與出口通路）的能力。透過持續的產品創新，我們致力於迎合不斷變化的消費者偏好，包括對便利性與小份量的需求，以及對新口味與多樣化風味的興趣。我們也致力於利用出口市場作為提升原料價值的通路，透過整隻豬的利用，並迎合差異化、全球化的口味與偏好。

我們的營運成本佔銷售額的百分比會根據原料價格波動，以及製造、運輸與行銷成本而變化。原料為我們總成本中最大的零組件，其中飼料原料與豬隻佔據絕大多數的比重。飼料原料、豬隻與豬肉的價格會根據市場動態而波動，這可能會影響我們的毛利率。此外，我們的運輸成本會受到燃料價格的影響，而燃料價格也會根據市場動態而波動，可能導致飼料原料及其他投入成本的價格上漲。當我們認為條件適當時，我們會進行飼料原料、豬隻與燃料等商品的避險交易，以降低內在的價格風險。雖然這種避險可能限制我們參與有利商品價格波動的獲利機會，但也會降低原料價格不利變動所導致的損失風險。
我們持續優化豬隻生產作業的規模，並從獨立供應商處採購更多以市場為基礎的豬隻，以供應我們的鮮豬肉分部。我們已將內部豬隻生產規模從2019年的高峯17.6百萬頭減少至2025年的11.1百萬頭，這相當於我們鮮豬肉分部處理豬隻數量的大約40%。我們持續探討在中長期內進一步減少內部生產的機會。
我們在工廠內推行最佳製造原則，透過自動化重新配置勞動力至更高價值的任務，提高產出並推動效率，同時減少複雜性。在物流與運輸網路方面，我們透過改善電信業者組合、最大化冷儲存與卡車資產的使用率、改善供需規劃及優化存貨水準，來降低運輸與倉儲成本。
我們的營運成果將持續依賴我們的能力：(1) 透過優化豬隻生產作業、避險、預購、戰略採購談判及將通貨膨脹成本轉嫁給客戶，來管理原料成本的變動；(2) 有效且具競爭力地運作製造與物流設施；(3) 繼續透過有效的銷售與行銷支出來吸引並留住客戶與消費者。

headings: 與我們業務及運營相關的風險
我們的營運結果具有週期性，可能因肉類、畜牧產品（主要為豬隻）及飼料原料的價格波動而受到不利影響。
供應鏈中斷可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。
無法實現節省成本與效率提升，可能影響利潤，我們可能無法達成任何或全部的財務與運營目標。
消費者偏好變動及未能維持對我們品牌與產品的正面消費者觀感，可能對我們的業務造成負面影響。
畜牧產品中傳染病的爆發可能顯著影響生產、原材料供應、我們產品的需求以及業務。
產品責任索償或產品回收事件可能對我們的企業聲譽造成不利影響，使我們面臨聯邦及州政府監管機構更嚴格的審查，且可能未被保險覆蓋。
本公司對第三方服務供應商之依賴，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
因應季節性或促銷活動之變動，本公司營業收入與營運成果可能於各季度間有所差異。
分銷成本顯著增加，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司營運面臨與併購、合資企業投資及資產處分相關之風險。
本公司面臨與國際銷售相關之風險，包括因美國貿易政策變動而導致全球經濟動盪。
本公司依賴員工之可得性及與員工之良好關係。
本公司面臨與員工就業及健康安全相關之各項風險。
本公司依賴高階管理團隊中某些關鍵成員之持續服務，若無這些成員，本公司業務營運可能產生顯著影響
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中，應謹慎考量。上述任何風險或未知風險與不確定性之發生，可能對本公司之業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
本風險因素總覽為本公司業務相關風險之高階總結。此總覽並未包含所有對您可能重要的資訊，您應配合此風險因素總覽，閱讀後續更詳細說明之風險與不確定性。本公司風險總覽包括但不限於下列項目：
•本公司營運結果具有週期性，可能因肉類、畜牧產品（主要為豬隻）及飼料原料之商品價格波動而受到不利影響。
•本公司供應鏈之中斷可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。
•無法實現節省與效率提升之情形，可能影響利潤率，且本公司可能無法達成任何或全部之財務與營運目標。
•本公司所屬之食品產業為高度競爭產業，若本公司無法成功競爭，或因競爭而產生之影響，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。
